done_state: tessera/reviewui/static/ is a live-updating HTML/JS/CSS page (served by api, talking only to api) showing open bugs/todos and a diff-vs-claim view that surfaces api's computed discrepancy prominently, with explicit-save doc editing (verified no network write before Save is clicked) and HTML-escaped rendering of all agent-generated content -- all demonstrated in a real headless-browser session against a real running server, not asserted from reading the JS.

criteria.statement: The open bugs/todos view, loaded in a real headless browser against a real running tessera server, displays ticket data actually fetched from the API (not hardcoded/mock content).

The diff-vs-claim view, for a ticket with a deliberately-mismatched claim (claims fewer files than the real diff touched), visibly surfaces the discrepancy (a distinct, non-hidden DOM element listing the mismatched files) rather than requiring a human to compare two panels unaided.
The diff-vs-claim view for a MATCHING claim shows no discrepancy element flagged as a mismatch (no false positive) -- both the positive and negative case are demonstrated in the same browser session.

A ticket whose title/comment contains HTML/script content is rendered escaped: no JavaScript dialog fires (proving no script execution) and the raw '<script>' text is not present unescaped in the rendered DOM.

Editing a doc's content in the browser and NOT clicking Save results in zero PUT requests to /docs/*; clicking Save results in exactly one, with the edited content -- proving no autosave-on-blur/interval exists.
The SSE connection indicator shows connected on page load, and a ticket created by a genuinely separate OS process appears in the open list without a page reload, within the poll interval.
The server response for reviewui's page sends a Content-Security-Policy header restricting script sources.

failure_criteria.statement: The escaping guard only covers ticket titles, not comments/claim summaries -- an XSS vector remains in a field that was not tested.
failure_criteria.detection: C4's test injects the payload into both a ticket title AND a comment body.

failure_criteria.statement: A claim about the UI's behavior (e.g. 'live-updating') is asserted without a real browser session proving it.
failure_criteria.detection: Every criterion here is verified against a real headless-browser session against a real running server (reviewui_browser_check.py), not by reading the JS source and reasoning about what it should do.

failure_criteria.statement: reviewui writes to store, gitops, or the filesystem directly, bypassing api -- the single-write-path design ARCHITECTURE.md specifies is violated.
failure_criteria.detection: grep tessera/reviewui/static/*.js for any URL that isn't a call to the api's own HTTP endpoints; there should be none.

failure_criteria.statement: A fetch() error (e.g. the API being down) is caught and silently ignored, leaving the UI looking fine while showing stale/wrong data.
failure_criteria.detection: The SSE/fetch error paths update the visible connection-status indicator, not just console.log.

out_of_scope: A JS build pipeline / bundler / framework (React, Vue, etc.) -- plain HTML/CSS/JS only, matching the stdlib-only, fewer-moving-parts architecture.
User accounts / per-user preferences (no auth in scope).
constraints: No third-party JS libraries or CDN scripts (CSP + no-network-dependency constraints from ARCHITECTURE.md/SCOPE.md).
Talks only to api (reviewui_to_api / api_to_reviewui edges) -- never store, gitops, or the filesystem directly.
All dynamic content insertion goes through a single escaping helper, not scattered innerHTML assignments.

Real bugs caught by running this in an actual browser rather than reading the JS: (1) JS boolean String(data.matches) stringifies lowercase ('false'/'true'), the test's own assertion wrongly expected Python-style capitalization; (2) reviewui's own CSP (script-src 'self', no unsafe-eval) blocks Playwright's string-based wait_for_function, which needs in-page eval -- fixed by polling from the Python side instead of weakening the CSP, since the CSP doing exactly this is a correct security property, not a bug.

amendments.reason: Real browser verification requires Playwright, which is not installed for /usr/bin/python3 or this project's own environment (this project is stdlib-only by ARCHITECTURE.md's own constraint, and Playwright is verification tooling, not a product dependency). The existing latent-loop-verify tool's venv already has Playwright installed and is the appropriate interpreter for this one-time build-verification step.
